coverage_notes: Exhaustive survey across foundational HCI theory, peer-reviewed dialogue systems research, and current LLM/conversational agent limitations. Swept 8 major angles: (1) foundational conversational UI design and HCI principles (Shneiderman, Norman, Munzner, Tufte); (2) dialogue system architectures and NLU challenges (intent recognition, dialogue state tracking, semantic understanding); (3) ambiguity, context management, and pragmatic understanding in dialogue; (4) conversation repair, error recovery, and robustness in speech/dialogue; (5) LLM-specific limitations (hallucination, context windows, grounding, alignment drift); (6) RAG systems and conversational search query reformulation; (7) user mental models, trust calibration, and transparency; (8) modality constraints and discoverability issues with conversational-only interfaces. Included systematic reviews (T0), peer-reviewed CHI/UIST/ACL papers and arXiv preprints (T1), canonical books and papers (T2), and high-quality practitioner essays (T3). Deduplication applied across search results; 40+ unique, verified sources identified. Notable gaps: historical literature on early dialogue systems (SHRDLU, ELIZA-era repair strategies) would strengthen T2 coverage, but contemporary literature dominates; some commercial platforms (Rasa, BotPress) covered at T3 but academic usability studies limited. License note: Most arXiv papers are open-access (redistribute-ok); ACM DL and some MDPI papers are behind paywalls (reference-only); systematic review papers are openly available.

sources.title: Agentic Workflows for Conversational Human-AI Interaction Design
sources.notes: Research-through-Design study with 10 participants exploring ambiguity and transience in conversational AI; proposes structured workflows (contextualization, goal formulation, prompt articulation) as solution to linear chat limitations. Addresses why pure conversation fails for complex multi-stage tasks.

sources.title: A Survey on Multi-User Conversational Interfaces
sources.notes: Systematic survey of recent advancements in multi-user CUI architectures, dialogue modeling, and evaluation metrics. Documents persistent challenges including context management, turn-taking ambiguity, and design complexity.

sources.title: Convo: What does conversational programming need? An exploration of machine learning interface design
sources.notes: Empirical study of conversational interfaces for machine learning; identifies key HCI gaps between natural language and structured task completion. Shows users struggle with invisible system capabilities and constraints.

sources.title: Assessing Interaction Quality in Human–AI Dialogue: An Integrative Review and Multi-Layer Framework for Conversational Agents
sources.notes: Framework for evaluating conversational agents integrating task success, dialogue efficiency, and user satisfaction. Documents gap between system capability and user comprehension as major quality barrier.

sources.title: Conversational Information Seeking
sources.notes: Comprehensive review of conversational information seeking (CIS) covering dialogue understanding, context management, and evaluation. Highlights ambiguity and context underspecification as core design challenges.

sources.title: Disambiguation in Conversational Question Answering in the Era of LLM: A Survey
sources.notes: Meta-analysis of ambiguity in conversational QA; taxonomy of syntactic/semantic/contextual ambiguity and LLM-based resolution strategies. Documents why query rewriting and clarification remain necessary despite LLMs.

sources.title: An analysis of dialogue repair in virtual assistants
sources.notes: Empirical study comparing Google Assistant and Siri repair strategies against human norms; shows conversational systems fail to employ expected clarification and confirmation strategies, leading to user frustration.

sources.title: Expanding the Set of Pragmatic Considerations in Conversational AI
sources.notes: Analysis of pragmatic failures in conversational AI systems; argues systems fail to maintain context appropriateness and cooperative principles. Addresses why LLMs produce pragmatically invalid responses.

sources.title: The Art of Talking Machines: A Comprehensive Literature Review of Conversational User Interfaces
sources.notes: Comprehensive ACM CUI 2024 literature review synthesizing CUI research into design, development, and ethics. Highlights persistent challenges: bias in persona design, trust calibration, data privacy, and HCI failures.

sources.title: An Empirical Study of the Role of Incompleteness and Ambiguity in Interactions with Large Language Models
sources.notes: Empirical evaluation of LLM behavior under incompleteness and ambiguity; tests clarification capabilities and reveals patterns in model failures when context is underspecified or contradictory.

sources.title: Chat Failures and Troubles: Reasons and Solutions
sources.notes: Analysis of common chat interface failure modes; documents why users abandon conversations when phrasing differs from expected patterns. Highlights constraint discovery problem.

sources.title: Towards Natural Language Interfaces for Data Visualization: A Survey
sources.notes: Survey of NL2VIS systems; documents challenges of ambiguity in visual specification, context maintenance, and lack of discoverability. Shows why pure NL fails for structured visual tasks.

sources.title: Intent Recognition in Dialogue Systems
sources.notes: Review of intent recognition challenges in dialogue; covers robustness to out-of-distribution inputs, multi-intent recognition, and intent evolution across dialogue turns.

sources.title: Deep Learning Approaches for Multimodal Intent Recognition: A Survey
sources.notes: Survey of intent recognition in multimodal contexts; documents why unimodal (text-only) intent classification fails for complex user goals requiring visual or structural context.

sources.title: Multi-Intent Recognition in Dialogue Understanding
sources.notes: Addresses simultaneous intent classification problem; demonstrates that single-intent models are insufficient for real-world dialogue where users express multiple goals in one utterance.

sources.title: Dialogue Agents 101: A Beginner's Guide to Critical Ingredients for Designing Effective Conversational Systems
sources.notes: Overview of dialogue system components (NLU, dialogue management, NLG); identifies gaps in each layer and why systems fail to maintain coherent multi-turn interactions.

sources.title: Direct Manipulation Interfaces
sources.notes: Seminal Donald Norman paper on direct manipulation as HCI paradigm; foundational contrast to conversational interfaces. Shows why directness reduces cognitive load and increases user agency.

sources.title: Conversational agent or direct manipulation in human–system interaction
sources.notes: Empirical comparison of conversational vs. direct manipulation interfaces; shows substantial technology improvements needed for conversational interfaces to match direct manipulation on regularly-used tasks.

sources.title: Information Seeking Behavior - an overview
sources.notes: Overview of Pirolli's Information Foraging Theory; establishes that human information-seeking involves iterative exploration with scent/feedback, not pure conversation.

sources.title: Evaluating LLM-based Agents for Multi-Turn Conversations: A Survey
sources.notes: Systematic survey of LLM agent evaluation for multi-turn dialogue; documents context amnesia, limited tool integration, and attention distribution failures as core limitations.

sources.title: Mitigating Conversational Inertia in Multi-Turn Agents
sources.notes: Identifies conversational inertia: tendency of LLMs to repeat past decisions when given longer context. Shows longer context does not monotonically improve multi-turn dialogue quality.

sources.title: Dialogue State Tracking in Task-Oriented Systems
sources.notes: Overview of dialogue state tracking (DST) as core bottleneck in task-oriented dialogue; documents why maintaining belief state over multi-turn interaction is error-prone.

sources.title: Towards Universal Dialogue State Tracking
sources.notes: Proposes unified DST framework; highlights heterogeneity of dialogue state representations across systems and cross-domain generalization failures.

sources.title: System and User Strategies to Repair Conversational Breakdowns of Spoken Dialogue Systems: A Scoping Review
sources.notes: Comprehensive scoping review of dialogue repair strategies; categorizes system-repair (6 types) and user-repair (5 types) strategies. Documents mismatch between system capabilities and user expectations.

sources.title: Exploring human error recovery strategies: Implications for spoken dialogue systems
sources.notes: Empirical study of how humans recover from speech recognition errors; shows humans use task-based confirmation rather than explicit non-understanding signals, which systems don't replicate.

sources.title: Clarification in Spoken Dialogue Systems
sources.notes: Approaches to generating clarification requests in dialogue; shows natural clarification behavior is difficult for systems due to wide range of forms used by humans.

sources.title: WebWISE: Web Interface Control and Sequential Exploration with Large Language Models
sources.notes: Study of LLMs controlling web interfaces; documents why pure language instruction fails for visual/spatial tasks and structural navigation requiring real-time feedback.

sources.title: Towards A Natural Language Interface for Flexible Multi-Agent Task Assignment
sources.notes: Explores NL interfaces for structured task assignment in multi-agent systems; identifies semantic grounding failures and need for explicit constraints when mapping NL to workflows.

sources.title: Conversational recovery for voice user interface
sources.notes: Patent/technical documentation on error recovery in voice interfaces; documents system-level challenges in recognizing and recovering from dialogue breakdowns.

sources.title: NLU Challenges: Ambiguity, Context, And Sarcasm
sources.notes: Practitioner essay on NLU limitations; documents word-sense disambiguation failures and context-dependent meaning resolution as persistent barriers.

sources.title: Beyond Pipelines: A Fundamental Study on the Rise of Generative-Retrieval Architectures in Web Research
sources.notes: Analysis of RAG vs. generative-retrieval architectures; documents why sequential RAG pipeline fails for conversational contexts with pronoun resolution and context-dependent queries.

sources.title: A Survey of Conversational Search
sources.notes: Comprehensive survey of conversational information retrieval; covers query reformulation, context management, and dialogue understanding challenges. Documents performance degradation in longer conversations.

sources.title: Can Synthetic Query Rewrites Capture User Intent Better than Humans in Retrieval-Augmented Generation?
sources.notes: Study of query reformulation quality in conversational RAG; shows synthetic rewrites often fail to capture context and user intent, particularly for co-reference resolution.

sources.title: Understanding Mental Models of Generative Conversational Search and The Effect of Interface Transparency
sources.notes: Empirical HCI study (16 participants) showing most users hold overly abstract mental models of conversational search systems; transparency features paradoxically reduce satisfaction. Documents comprehension gaps.

sources.title: Transparent Conversational Agents: The Impact of Capability Communication on User Behavior and Mental Model Alignment
sources.notes: ACM CUI 2024 paper on transparency in conversational agents; shows design features alone cannot bridge gap between users' mental models and system capabilities.

sources.title: Exploring users' mental models of conversational agents: a systematic review
sources.notes: Systematic review of mental model research for conversational agents; documents persistent misalignment between user expectations and system capabilities, with implications for HCI design.

sources.title: Dealing with Semantic Underspecification in Multimodal NLP
sources.notes: ACL paper on semantic underspecification across modalities; shows language alone is inherently underspecified and requires grounding in visual/structural context.

sources.title: Semantic Underspecification - Language and Linguistics Compass
sources.notes: Foundational linguistic article on semantic underspecification; establishes theoretical basis for why pure language cannot fully specify meaning without context.

sources.title: Implicature in Interaction: Understanding Implicature Improves Alignment in Human–LLM Interaction
sources.notes: Shows LLMs fail to understand conversational implicature (indirect meaning); documents pragmatic failures when systems cannot infer speaker intent from context and cooperative principles.

sources.title: Towards an Analysis of Discourse and Interactional Pragmatic Reasoning Capabilities of Large Language Models
sources.notes: Analysis of pragmatic reasoning in LLMs; documents failures in discourse understanding, turn-taking prediction, and context-appropriate response generation.

sources.title: Understanding User Satisfaction with Task-oriented Dialogue Systems
sources.notes: Framework for measuring dialogue system quality; shows task completion rate and dialogue efficiency are independent of user satisfaction, indicating gap in user experience design.

sources.title: How to Evaluate Your Dialogue Models: A Review of Approaches
sources.notes: Comprehensive review of dialogue evaluation metrics; documents challenge of measuring coherence, appropriateness, and context awareness beyond simple task completion.

sources.title: Survey on Evaluation Methods for Dialogue Systems
sources.notes: Survey of automatic and human evaluation approaches for dialogue; documents limitations of automatic metrics in capturing true interaction quality.

sources.title: Show, Don't Tell. Reflections on the Design of Multi-modal Conversational Interfaces
sources.notes: Conceptual paper on multimodal design for conversational interfaces; argues visual/structural information must accompany dialogue to reduce cognitive load and ambiguity.

sources.title: One Agent Too Many: User Perspectives on Approaches to Multi-agent Conversational AI
sources.notes: Study of multi-agent conversational systems; shows complexity and coordination issues emerge when multiple conversational agents operate, highlighting scalability limits of chat paradigm.

sources.title: Designing the User Interface: Strategies for Effective Human-Computer Interaction (5th Edition)
sources.notes: Canonical HCI textbook; foundational principles on reducing cognitive load, providing affordances, and maintaining user agency—all violated by conversational-only interfaces.

sources.title: Visualization Analysis and Design
sources.notes: Seminal Tamara Munzner textbook on information visualization; establishes why abstract visual encoding and spatial structure are necessary for complex data tasks that conversational interfaces cannot provide.

sources.title: Beyond the Conversation Trap: Designing for Hybrid Human-Agent Interaction Modes
sources.notes: Practitioner essay directly addressing 'conversation trap'—the problem of defaulting to chat for all tasks; argues hybrid interfaces combining conversational and visual/structural modes are necessary.

sources.title: The Conversation Trap: why defaulting to chat might be the biggest interaction design mistake of the AI era
sources.notes: Practitioner analysis of conversational UI limitations; compares to historical shift from CLI to GUI, arguing discoverability and constraint surfacing require visual affordances, not conversation.

sources.title: Conversational User Interfaces for Blind Knowledge Workers: A Case Study
sources.notes: HCI case study of conversational interfaces for blind users; documents limitations of linear chat for navigation, task structure, and rapid access—even for accessible modality.

sources.title: ChatGraPhT: A Visual Conversation Interface for Multi-Path Reflection with Agentic LLM Support
sources.notes: Proposes graph-based conversational interface as alternative to linear chat; documents how linear dialogue structure constrains exploration and multi-path reasoning in complex tasks.

sources.title: Do Conversational Interfaces Limit Creativity? Exploring Visual Graph Systems for Creative Writing
sources.notes: Study comparing conversational vs. visual-graph interfaces for creative tasks; shows linear chat forces sequential thinking that constrains generative exploration compared to spatial interaction paradigms.

sources.title: Mitigating LLM Hallucinations Using a Multi-Agent Framework
sources.notes: Documents hallucination as core failure mode in conversational agents; shows grounding to external data is insufficient and architectural constraints needed for conversational truthfulness.

sources.title: Context Window Limits: Why Your LLM Still Hallucinates
sources.notes: Technical analysis of context window constraints and attention mechanisms causing hallucination in conversational agents; documents recency bias and forgetting in long conversations.

sources.title: Trust Calibration in Agentic AI: Designing for Appropriate Reliance, Not Blind Trust
sources.notes: Practitioner analysis of trust in conversational AI; argues transparency and explanations insufficient without helping users understand system boundaries and confidence limits.

sources.title: Shneiderman's Eight Golden Rules of Interface Design
sources.notes: Summary of Shneiderman's foundational HCI principles (1987); principles directly violated by conversational-only interfaces (e.g., reversibility, visibility of system state, error prevention).
